overview: The two functionally distinct regions of the adrenal gland, one steroid-hormone-producing and the other a modified sympathetic nerve tissue.
genZNote: Adrenal cortex: the slow-and-steady steroid factory on the outside. Adrenal medulla: the fast 'fight or flight' alarm bell at the core.

aspects.label: Hormones Produced
aspects.valueA: Corticosteroids: cortisol (glucocorticoid), aldosterone (mineralocorticoid), and some androgens.

aspects.label: Embryonic Origin
aspects.valueB: Derived from neural crest cells — essentially a modified sympathetic ganglion.

aspects.label: Speed of Response
aspects.valueB: Rapid-acting, short-duration effects, central to the acute stress response.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The adrenal medulla is developmentally a modified sympathetic ganglion, which is why adrenaline acts so similarly to a neurotransmitter.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cortex = corticosteroids, slow. Medulla = fight-or-flight, fast.
overlay.commonMisconception: Adrenaline is not made in the adrenal cortex — cortisol and adrenaline come from two structurally and developmentally distinct parts of the same gland.
